questions.q: In "Know your guests and the rules Define", which of these is a key idea?
o: Group guests into families, couples, solo travellers, friend groups and work travellers, and list what each needs.
Give a printed guest guide with the emergency numbers, nearest hospital and Wi-Fi details.
Work out occupancy: nights sold divided by nights available.
Check gas cylinder, regulator, geyser and wiring for faults before every season, and switch off the gas at the cylinder when not in use.

questions.q: In "Prepare a safe and clean space Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Group guests into families, couples, solo travellers, friend groups and work travellers, and list what each needs.
Keep a first aid box, fire extinguisher, torch and a list of local emergency numbers in view.
Prepare the property and pass the 30-point check.
Send directions, check-in time and a contact number two days before arrival.

questions.q: In "Furnish and stock for comfort Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Reply to every enquiry within two hours with dates, price, rules and what is included.
List the basics per room: bed, two pillows, two sets of sheets, towels, curtains, hooks, a bin with a lid.
Work out average daily rate: income divided by nights sold.
Check the room with the guest at check-out and note damage on the same day.

questions.q: In "Set prices that fit Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Prepare the property and pass the 30-point check.
Send directions, check-in time and a contact number two days before arrival.
Check what three similar places nearby charge in each season.
Clean in order: top to bottom, dry to wet, and change all linen between guests.

questions.q: In "Take bookings and communicate Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Publish the price table and take a booking from enquiry to check-out.
Write the guest guide and a risk list with actions.
Group guests into families, couples, solo travellers, friend groups and work travellers, and list what each needs.
Send directions, check-in time and a contact number two days before arrival.

questions.q: In "Run check-in, stay and check-out Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Give a printed guest guide with the emergency numbers, nearest hospital and Wi-Fi details.
Collect guest ID as the law requires and store it safely.
Set a base rate, then a peak rate, a low rate and a weekly discount.
List seasons in your area: peak, shoulder and low, with school-holiday and festival dates.

questions.q: In "Track income, costs and reviews Analyse", which of these is a key idea?
o: Work out average daily rate: income divided by nights sold.
Walk the property with a 30-point checklist: locks, lights, water, power, stairs, balcony rails, mattresses, bathrooms, kitchen.
Add extra charges clearly: extra bed, extra guest, cooking gas, firewood.
Check the room with the guest at check-out and note damage on the same day.

questions.q: In "Capstone: a full booking cycle Create", which of these is a key idea?
o: Walk the property with a 30-point checklist: locks, lights, water, power, stairs, balcony rails, mattresses, bathrooms, kitchen.
Greet the guest, collect ID, show the rooms and explain water, power, gas and house rules.
Present the month report and a plan for the next season.
Check what three similar places nearby charge in each season.
